name: URL State

hero.title: Refresh. Paste the link. The filters are still there.
hero.lede: `useUrlState('page', 1)` is a signal that lives in the address bar, typed from its default. Search, sort, tabs and pagination survive a reload, a shared link and the back button, with no parsers to write and no adapter to mount.

items.title: Typed by its default
items.text: `useUrlState('page', 1)` returns a number, `useUrlState('inStock', false)` a boolean, `useUrlState('tags', [] as string[])` an array. `?tags=a,b` reads back as `['a', 'b']`.

items.title: Clean URLs by default
items.text: A value equal to its default leaves the URL, so `sort=name` never shows up. Set `clearOnDefault: false` to keep it.

items.title: Back and forward just work
items.text: A `popstate` updates every signal bound to that key and re-runs what reads it. Two components on the same key stay in sync.

items.title: One history write per click
items.text: Writes use `replaceState` unless you ask for `push`. `batchUrlUpdates(() => { … })` folds several params into one history operation; `debounce: 300` keeps a search box from writing on every key.

difference.title: The parsers come from your defaults.

before.label: React + nuqs 2
before.caption: A parser per param, a tuple per hook, and an adapter at the root.

after.label: with @pyreon/url-state
after.caption: Each param is a signal. The default says the type. Only the text that reads it updates.

comingFrom.title: Parsers become defaults; setters become `.set()`.
comingFrom.note: nuqs ships more built-in parsers (dates, string literals, enums). Here those are a `serialize`/`deserialize` pair on the option, and a plain object default goes through JSON on its own. Both libraries drop a param that equals its default.

demo.title: Change filters, watch the URL.
demo.text: Every control is a URL-synced signal. Defaults disappear from the address bar.
demo.referenceHtml: Page 1

items.name: Schema mode
items.text: `useUrlState({ q: '', sort: 'name' })` returns one signal per key.

items.name: Type coercion
items.text: Numbers, floats, booleans and arrays come back as their types, not strings.

items.name: Arrays two ways
items.text: `?tags=a,b` (default, commas inside a value escaped) or `arrayFormat: 'repeat'` for `?tags=a&tags=b`.

items.name: `clearOnDefault`
items.text: On by default: the URL holds only what differs from the default.

items.name: `debounce`
items.text: One URL write after the user stops typing.

items.name: `replace: false`
items.text: Use `pushState` when a change deserves its own back-button step.

items.name: `onChange`
items.text: Fires on back/forward, router navigation or another hook writing the same key, never for your own `.set()`.

items.name: `setUrlRouter`
items.text: Route writes through `@pyreon/router` (or anything with `replace(path)`) so guards and scroll handling stay in charge.

recipes.title: A product list you can link to
recipes.text: Search, sort, a stock filter and the page number, all in the URL. Changing the search resets the page in the same history write.

recipes.title: Tabs that survive a reload
recipes.text: A tab is a string param. The default tab keeps the URL clean; every other tab is shareable.

limits.title: The server renders the default
limits.text: On the server every signal starts at its default; it does not read the request URL. A server-rendered page linked with `?page=3` shows page 1 until the client takes over, so read the param in your loader when the first paint must match.

limits.title: With a router set, the router writes
limits.text: After `setUrlRouter(router)`, a write is `router.replace(url)`, or `router.push(url)` for a signal with `replace: false`. A router without `push` falls back to `replace` and warns once.

limits.title: Complex values need a serializer
limits.text: Dates and enums take a `serialize`/`deserialize` pair; a plain object default is stored as JSON. Keep the URL for what a user would share; put the rest in a store.

limits.title: The address bar is a web thing
limits.text: On iOS and Android (experimental), `useUrlState` with a literal key and a string, number or boolean default binds to the native router's query; literal-array defaults join them in the next release. An object default stays web with a named warning, and `debounce`, `clearOnDefault: false` and custom serializers have no effect there.

faq.q: Does every keystroke add a history entry?
faq.a: No. Writes default to `replaceState`, and `debounce` delays the write until typing stops. Pass `replace: false` only where the back button should step through changes.

faq.q: What if the URL holds garbage, like `?page=abc`?
faq.a: A value that does not parse as the default's type falls back to the default: `?page=abc` reads as 1, `?inStock=yes` as false. For stricter rules, pass a `deserialize`.

On parsing, mostly: boolean 1.8×, array parse 2.1×, array serialize 1.2×, float 1.7×. Integer parse is 1.1× slower (8.1 vs 7.0 ns), and string, number serialize and round-trip tie. One run, bun, nanoseconds either way.
No. Without one it writes to `history` directly. With `@pyreon/router`, call `setUrlRouter(router)` once so router navigation and URL state stay in step.

benchmarks.p: The codec work that runs on every read and write: parse the param, serialize it back. Wins on booleans, floats and arrays; integer parse is a nanosecond behind; three rows tie.
